To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a set of QTL clusters affecting grain shape and/or chalkiness traits and have identified a set co-localized candidate genes for chalkiness.

the high-resolution QTL mapping and transcriptome analysis of rice grain appearance traits were carried out, and co-localization between chalkiness-related QTM clusters and candidate genes was detected.

the genetic architecture of grain shape and chalkness in rice were revealed using high-density GBS markers, and the important DEGs were co-localized nearby the QTL clusters affecting grain shape and endopserm chalkiness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic dissection and gene expression profiling of grain appearance traits, which is helpful to understand the genetic basis of grain appearance quality and chalkiness in rice.

a novel approach to identify and characterize the QTLs for grain shape and chalkness traits, and the results provide a basis for the future fine mapping and molecular cloning of chalkiness-associated genes.

the genetic basis of grain quality in rice, and the results are expected to be of great significance for further functional studies of the chalkiness-associated candidate genes and for breeding programs of rice grain quality improvement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genetic architecture of grain shape and chalky endosperm traits are complex and controlled by a large number of QTLs with small to moderate effect, and the co-localization of DEGs and QTLs provides an opportunity to identify candidate genes for further functional validation and breeding application.
the genetic architecture of grain shape and chalkness in rice is complex and the QTLs affecting these traits are located in the genome regions of cloned genes and/or fine-mapped QTLs.

the high-resolution genetic map and QTL analysis based on the RILs population derived from PYZX × P02428 cross is a valuable tool for further functional validation of the candidate genes, and for the breeding of high-quality rice cultivars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high-resolution QTL mapping and co-localization with DEGs could be a useful approach for the genetic dissection of grain appearance quality traits in rice.
we have successfully developed an efficient and high-resolution QTL mapping strategy, which is applicable for the genetic dissection of complex traits in rice and other crops.
the GBS-based QTL mapping and transcriptome analysis are efficient approaches for the identification of QTL clusters and candidate genes affecting rice grain quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the high-density genetic map and the QTLs for grain appearance quality can provide a valuable genetic resource for the molecular dissection of grain quality, and the identified candidate genes are useful for further functional characterization and breeding utilization.
the GBS approach is a promising tool to construct a high-density genetic linkage map, and to dissect the genetic basis of grain appearance quality traits in rice.
the GBS-SNP approach is a promising method for QTL mapping and transcriptome analysis, and the high-density genetic map is a useful tool for fine mapping and map-based cloning of the important genes.
